title: Recording: Let ’Em In, Cook Of The House by Wings | 1976
content:
7 Cavendish Avenue, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Peter Henderson

Wings recorded effects for the Wings At The Speed Of Sound songs ‘Let ’Em In’ and ‘Cook Of The House’ on 19 February 1976.

The session, unusually, took place at Paul and Linda McCartney’s London home, 7 Cavendish Avenue, a short walk from Abbey Road. It was recorded using EMI’s Mobile Unit.

Harmonium pieces were recorded, to be used between ‘She’s My Baby’ and ‘Beware My Love’, and ‘Time To Hide’ and ‘Must Do Something About It’.

Paul McCartney then decided to record the sound of a doorbell, to open ‘Let ’Em In’. The doorbell had been a gift from drummer Joe English.

The final effects were the noise of bacon and chips being fried.

Paul and Linda decided to cook a meal and get cooking sounds recorded, and then fed the meal to us and the engineers,” said Peter. “We all had a laugh and a drink. The mobile was outside the house, and we just ran wires into the kitchen. ‘Take one. Bacon frying.’ The first British cooking on record. There are chips [frying] at the end which is great because it sounds like applause.
Peter Henderson
Melody Maker, 27 March 1976

Three tape reels were filled. The first two had the harmonium links, and the third – marked ‘One Wild Piece’/‘Cook Of The House’ – contained the doorbell and kitchen sounds.
